skill.name: email-sequence-designer
skill.description: Designs lifecycle email flows with triggers, timing, branches, exits, frequency controls, sunset rules, and SEND N scoring.
skill.summary: Plan coordinated email sequences before writing or scheduling individual messages.
skill.author: aaron-he-zhu

security_audit.summary: One finding is confirmed: line 52 directs execution of a connector command that can schedule a live email broadcast. The other 45 findings are false positives from Markdown formatting, links, metadata, and a constrained output path. No prompt injection, credential theft, obfuscation, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: The skill can invoke a connector with --live to send email broadcasts.
remediation.suggestion: Keep preview mode mandatory, require explicit confirmation immediately before --live, validate recipient consent, and restrict command arguments to structured values.

content.value_statement: Disconnected email flows cause missed conversions, fatigue, and compliance risk. This skill maps triggers, timing, branches, exits, frequency limits, and sunset rules for coordinated lifecycle programs.
actual_capabilities: Designs welcome, cart, browse-abandon, post-purchase, re-engagement, and cold-outbound flow maps.
Defines triggers, ordered steps, delays, goals, branches, and conversion or unsubscribe exits for each flow.
Sets global send caps, quiet hours, fatigue controls, and engagement-based sunset rules.
Scores the SEND N dimension for a selected promotional, retention, cold-outbound, or newsletter profile.
Produces a handoff summary for email copy creation and quality auditing.
limitations: Does not write final subject lines, body copy, preheaders, or calls to action.
Does not compute the complete EQS or enforce final unsubscribe vetoes.
Requires the user to confirm unknown triggers, segments, platform details, and consent status.
The package contains only SKILL.md, so referenced scripts and companion files are unavailable locally.

use_cases.title: Recover abandoned carts
use_cases.description: Map cart triggers, timed reminders, purchase exits, discount branches, and fatigue controls before creative production.

use_cases.title: Structure outbound follow-up
use_cases.description: Plan a multi-step B2B sequence with reply exits, segment relevance, timing, and global send limits.

use_cases.title: Govern lifecycle messaging
use_cases.description: Coordinate welcome, post-purchase, re-engagement, and sunset flows under one frequency policy and SEND N assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Create a welcome flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a welcome flow for [product] on [ESP]. Use [signup event] as the trigger and target [segment]. Map timing, goals, and exits.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new subscriber journey

prompt_templates.title: Plan cart recovery
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a [number]-step abandoned-cart sequence for [store]. Include delays, purchase exits, click branches, discount rules, send caps, and quiet hours.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a lifecycle portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit these existing lifecycle flows: [paste summary]. Identify missing flows and overlap. Propose governance, fatigue controls, sunset thresholds, and a SEND N score.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an established email program

prompt_templates.title: Design retention architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a retention lifecycle architecture for [business] using [data sources]. Map cross-flow progression, segment eligibility, suppression checks, global caps, and measured assumptions. Provide a handoff summary and flag inputs required from preference management or quality auditing.

output_examples.input: Design a three-step welcome flow for a subscription service.
output: Trigger: confirmed account creation for a new, consented subscriber.
Step 1: Send immediately with the activation goal.
Step 2: Send after two days if activation is incomplete.
Step 3: Send after five days if no key feature was used.
Exit on activation, unsubscribe, hard bounce, or suppression.

output_examples.input: Reduce fatigue across overlapping retail lifecycle flows.
output: Apply a maximum of three promotional emails per rolling seven days.
Pause lower-priority flows when cart recovery or service messaging is active.
Use local quiet hours and throttle subscribers after engagement declines.
Sunset subscribers after the confirmed inactivity window and consent review.

output_examples.input: Plan a B2B cold-outbound sequence with reply handling.
output: Enroll only the approved target segment with documented eligibility.
Use four steps across twelve business days with increasing value specificity.
Exit immediately on reply, unsubscribe, bounce, suppression, or account disqualification.
Mark timing and benchmark assumptions as estimated until campaign data is available.

best_practices: Confirm the trigger, target segment, consent state, and exit event before defining message timing.
Coordinate all flows under one send cap, quiet-hours policy, and fatigue response.
Label every recommendation as measured, user-provided, or estimated.
anti_patterns: Do not enroll suppressed or non-consented recipients in any lifecycle flow.
Do not let flows loop indefinitely without conversion, reply, unsubscribe, bounce, or sunset exits.
Do not schedule live broadcasts before previewing the request and receiving explicit confirmation.

faq.question: Does this skill write complete emails?
faq.answer: No. It designs the sequence structure and hands each step to a separate email creative workflow.

faq.question: Which lifecycle flows can it design?
faq.answer: It covers welcome, abandoned-cart, browse-abandon, post-purchase, replenishment, light re-engagement, and B2B cold-outbound flows.

faq.question: Can it score email quality?
faq.answer: It scores only the SEND N lifecycle dimension. A separate auditor must compute the complete EQS and enforce veto rules.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the flow goal, ESP, trigger event, target segment, current cadence, consent constraints, and available performance signals.

faq.question: Can it schedule email sends?
faq.answer: The source describes Resend connector commands, but this package does not include that connector. Live actions require preview and explicit confirmation.

faq.question: How does it prevent subscriber fatigue?
faq.answer: It defines global send caps, quiet hours, throttling rules, engagement checks, and a suppression or sunset path.
